summary: Perkins Island Light, a wooden tower on the Kennebec River lit in 1898 and automated in 1959; the tower is Coast Guard property leased to the American Lighthouse Foundation.

lens.where: fifth-order lens installed 1902, replaced by a 250 mm optic in 1979 (New England Lighthouses)

structures.note: Tapered octagonal frame, wood-shingled, on a stone foundation. Height: 23 ft (LighthouseFriends; USLHS base to lantern centre); the NRHP nomination gives 17 ft from base to lantern centre.
Two-storey L-shaped keeper's house, wood-shingled (NRHP). Owned by the State of Maine.
Pyramidal frame bell tower south of the light tower, with a 1,000-pound fog bell (NRHP; LighthouseFriends). Machinery by hand crank in the 1940s (LighthouseFriends).
Enclosed wooden boathouse with boat slip; LighthouseFriends says it was removed or destroyed at an unrecorded date.

access.note: Tower and dwelling closed. LighthouseFriends lists the grounds as open; the USLHS record says the station is not open to the public. Parker Head Road is marked private; LighthouseFriends advises viewing from the water.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard owns the tower, leased to the American Lighthouse Foundation; the State of Maine owns the dwelling

events.note: Lighthouse Board asks for a fixed red lens-lantern light with a white sector and a fog bell on the southwest point of Perkins Island
Act approved 2 March 1895 appropriates $17,000 for the Kennebec River lights
Title to the island acquired, plans prepared and contract let (reported in the Board's 1896-1897 report)
Tower, keeper's house and barn built
Light went into service in February 1898
White sector placed in the lantern on 10 July 1899
Gallery with railing built around the lantern; boat slip and landing steps built
Boathouse
Fifth-order Fresnel lens replaces the lens lantern, 15 January 1902 (LighthouseFriends)
Pyramidal bell tower with a 1,000-pound fog bell
Brick oil house
Keeper prevents a waterlogged rowboat loaded with lumber from capsizing; lumber saved (fiscal year 1916 table)
Keeper furnishes a party sheltering on the island during a thunderstorm with dry clothing and shelter (fiscal year 1916 table)
Launch caught fire with 20 people aboard on 29 August; keeper towed them to their destination
Keeper Eugene W. Osgood rescues a man from drowning in a sluiceway at Phippsburg, 16 June; commended by the Secretary of Commerce
Light automated
Buildings other than the tower transferred to the State of Maine in the 1960s
Fifth-order lens replaced by a 250 mm optic
Fog bell tower restored with Maine Department of Conservation and New Century Program grants
Coast Guard licenses the tower to the American Lighthouse Foundation (May 2000)
Crew restores and paints the keeper's dwelling, funded by a $45,000 local gift

corrections.proposed: Coast Guard owns the tower; leased to the American Lighthouse Foundation; State of Maine owns the dwelling; tower is federal
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says the tower is owned by the Coast Guard and leased to ALF, and the dwelling is owned by the State of Maine. The NRHP nomination says the tower was still maintained by the Coast Guard.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination gives 17 ft from base to centre of lantern; the USLHS record gives 23 ft from base to lantern centre; LighthouseFriends gives a 23-foot tower with focal plane 41 ft. Not reconciled; the story states the disagreement.

The 1892 Board report grouped four stations (Perkins Island, Squirrel Point, Doubling Point, Ames Ledge); LighthouseFriends counts five lights including Doubling Point Range. The NRHP nomination's 'four stations erected in 1898' is consistent with the first grouping.

LighthouseFriends says Coast Guard crews were assigned after Skolfield left in 1955, until automation in 1959, yet its own head-keeper list and the Archive both name Anthony Fargnoli (1956) and Robert Morong (1957). Stated in the story; not reconciled.
New England Lighthouses says Clifton Morong was keeper for several years in the 1940s (its list: c. 1941-1946); the Archive and LighthouseFriends give 1941 only. Stated in the story.
LighthouseFriends: Coast Guard owns the tower and leases it to the American Lighthouse Foundation; the Archive gives the Foundation as owner/manager. Stated in the story.

notes_for_editor: Sources and conflicts: (1) Haley's start: USLHS and LighthouseFriends say 1898; New England Lighthouses says 1911. The Board reports in our corpus for 1897-1901 do not name him, so 1898 is not confirmed by a primary source. (2) Tower height: NRHP 17 ft base to lantern centre; USLHS and LighthouseFriends 23 ft. (3) The 1916 table entries for Haley (sources 10 and 1): I matched the two services to the keeper by row order in the OCR'd table (rows 8 and 9 of the block), checked against LighthouseFriends' account; check the page image before publishing. (4) The 1902 fifth-order lens date (15 January 1902) rests on LighthouseFriends and New England Lighthouses; the 1902 Board report is not in the corpus. (5) The characteristic is not stated: the record gives Fl W 2.5s; Wikipedia (not cited; leads only) gives Fl R 2.5s with two white sectors citing the Light List. Verify against the current Light List before writing a characteristic. (6) The NRHP listing year (1988) is in our record and in Wikipedia but not in the nomination text, so no event is written for it. (7) Fog bell location: LighthouseFriends says Georgetown Central School; New England Lighthouses says Georgetown High School. (8) Access: USLHS says not open to the public; LighthouseFriends says grounds open, dwelling and tower closed. (9) Albert Orne is listed in USLHS under 'Contractor' with no dates; left out of the keeper roster. (10) Skolfield and Osgood family details are kept to public roles; Shirley and Ethel Morong/Osgood's children and Skolfield's family are not named. (11) LighthouseFriends is all rights reserved: facts and short quotes only; the 1941 Shirley Morong account and the 1955 Lewiston newspaper are second-hand, cited as LighthouseFriends quotes them. (12) Printed page numbers were not read from the page images: citations use Internet Archive scan pages. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22 (Haiku fact-checker): (a) The 1916 table (Commissioner's report, fiscal 1916, scan 165, printed p. 56) was read on the page image. J. W. Haley's row carries the 'Row boat' entry and the next row, marked 'do', carries the party sheltered during the thunderstorm, so both services belong to him; the matching by position is now confirmed. (b) Fiscal-year labels corrected: each Board report is 'for the fiscal year ended June 30' (1892, 1893, 1895, 1897, 1899, 1900). The Perkins title and contract entry is in the fiscal-1897 report (scan 294). (c) Shirley and Clifton Morong's account, Skolfield's life and the 1938 Osgood interview are all second-hand through LighthouseFriends and are footnoted to it. (d) Unresolved, not added to the roster: New England Lighthouses also names Irving T. Sparrow (Coast Guard, c. 1950s) and Charles L. Knight (?). Sparrow has no dates; Knight's 1935-book quotation describes a first station on the Kennebec that the sources do not name as Perkins Island. (e) Removed: 'Traffic on the lower Kennebec was heavy' (evaluative, not in source) and the advice that a visit should not include landing (not in any source). The 'best land view' reading of Parker Head Road is corrected: LighthouseFriends gives it as the route to a distant view from land, and says viewing from the water is the best option. (f) Units: 23 ft (7 m), 17 ft (5.2 m), 41 ft focal plane (12.5 m) added. (g) Citation fixes: 15 January 1902 is LighthouseFriends only; 'active aid' now cites the Archive and NEL, not the NRHP.
